title: BlendTree OneShots need an "abort if interrupted" flag
body: ### Tested versions Reproducible in current master, has been in 4 for as long as I can remember. ### System information Godot v4.5.1.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Single-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.8129) - AMD Ryzen 9 5950X 16-Core Processor (32 threads) - 63.91 GiB memory ### Issue description When a OneShot exists as part of a BlendTree state in a StateMachine, it attempts to fire soon as that state is entered and the OneShot is part of the blending. If that state is exited before the OneShot can complete its duration, then it continues over the course of fading transitions if any exist, and, failing that, pauses. Once the BlendTree is reentered, this OneShot proceeds to resume from wherever it reached. However, this "pausing" behaviour creates situations where the OneShot's purpose is antithetical to... being a one-time shot. If the OneShot is able to resume playback, that means manually having to manage every single OneShot to ensure abortion before reentering a state under different terms. For instance, I have a OneShot in my "crouch" BlendTree state, called "stop." This allows me to have the momentum from moving in the "sneak" state be settled all within the "crouch" idle state, which is at the moment more preferable than using a nested StateMachine to accomplish the same thing. However, if this settle animation is interrupted, without me making all of my transitions out of the "crouch" state long enough to accommodate its end, whenever I return to "crouch", even if under different terms, I am going to be subject to to that "stop" OneShot attempting to finish itself. In this video, I first "sneak" (moving), then enter "crouch" (idle), allowing the "stop" OneShot to reach its conclusion. Then, I move again, and once I stop moving, interrupt the "stop" OneShot to move, then transition into crawl, then come to a stop with my prone idle, then transition from the prone idle into my crouch idle again (also using a OneShot in the crouch state), but the prior "stop" OneShot with the wrong foot still tries to complete itself even though I moved on from it a long time ago. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0b20782d-69e8-4d32-819d-d13d1c8aca6f This was a far bigger problem in Godot 4 pre-#87171 (I think?), when the OneShot would actually restart from the beginning, every time it was interrupted and the state was reentered. I only realized improvements had been made to that recently, but was sticking with my extremely overkill method of ``` for oneshot in crouch_oneshots: animation_tree[oneshot + "/request"] = AnimationNodeOneShot.ONE_SHOT_REQUEST_ABORT ``` from earlier, to be safe. There NEEDS to be a way to force OneShots to always abort if it interrupted midway through. In my opinion, it should be the default. I cannot think of use cases for the current behaviour. If not, a boolean property on the node itself would be welcome. ### Steps to reproduce There's an MRP with an idle state, and an alternate state with a manually armed to fire OneShot. 1. Open MRP. 2. Run game. 3. Observe the idle state of spinning. 4. Hold spacebar to enter the state of spinning in the opposite direction, preceded by a OneShot of the box dropping down. 5. Interrupt this state by releasing spacebar. 6. Return to the state by holding spacebar again. 7. Repeat to observe troublesome behaviour. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [oneshot-interrupt.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23077757/oneshot-interrupt.zip)
